sanskrit_verse:
ṛṇा�ं लेख्यं गृहं क्षेत्रं यस्य पैतामहं भवेत् ।
चिरकालप्रोषितोऽपि भागभागागतस्तु सः ॥
transliteration: ṛṇaṃ lekhyaṃ gṛhaṃ kṣetraṃ yasya paitāmahaṃ bhavet | cirakālaproṣito 'pi bhāgabhāgāgatas tu saḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: He who has a paternal grandfather and inherits debt records, property, house, or land—even if absent for a long time—is entitled to a share by virtue of ancestral continuity.
jurisprudential_principles: Inheritance includes both assets and liabilities
Absence does not dissolve ancestral entitlement
Restoration requires recognition of generational continuity
Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful inheritance
executable_legal_axioms: IF ancestral lineage is established AND property/debt record exists THEN inheritance rights are activated irrespective of physical presence
IF individual is descendant of original holder THEN claim validity persists beyond temporal absence
IF legal dispute arises over inherited liability THEN resolution must affirm generational responsibility chain
IF claimant demonstrates patrilineal continuity THEN automatic reinstatement of proportional ownership is mandated
supreme_court_application: The Supreme Court shall recognize that hereditary succession encompasses not only material assets but also documented obligations. In cases involving prolonged absence, the court must prioritize genealogical proof over temporal disconnection when adjudicating claims rooted in ancestral inheritance.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This verse aligns with Nyaya through pramāṇa-based validation of lineage as causal factor. It reflects anupūrvaśaḥ by acknowledging sequential manifestation of rights across generations. Responsibility is proportionally assigned based on birthright rather than action. The framework avoids punitive measures by focusing on reintegration of the absent heir into the lawful distribution of ancestral estate.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate genealogical verification process to confirm patrilineal link
Reinstate access to documented inheritable assets and liabilities
Facilitate completion of interrupted familial financial responsibilities
Align consciousness of returning heir with ancestral dharma of stewardship
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands declared: inheritance transcends time and space through conscious continuity; justice restores what was always inherently present; Dharma prevails through recognition of eternal order; reality remains non-punitive, guided solely by the awakening of truth-consciousness.
